# Contribute {#contribute}

This is a wiki, which means it is meant to be added to. If you have a worked
example, a repository comparison, a language-specific gotcha, or a correction —
this page is how to get it in.

::: {.tada-key}
Copy [`templates/page-template.Rmd`](templates/page-template.Rmd), fill it in,
add the filename to `_bookdown.yml`, run `Rscript render.R`, and open a pull
request. The rest of this page is detail.
:::

## What belongs here {#contribute-scope}

**Yes, please:**

- Worked examples — a real README, a real project structure, a real code review
- Language- or tool-specific guidance (Julia, MATLAB, Stata, Snakemake…)
- Discipline-specific notes — TADA was developed in ecology and evolutionary
  biology, and the authors explicitly encourage adaptation to other fields
- Repository, licence or journal-policy information that has changed
- Corrections, especially anywhere this wiki has drifted from the source papers

**Probably not:**

- General programming tutorials — link to them from
  [Further reading](#further-reading) instead
- Advocacy for a particular statistical method
- Tool recommendations with no connection to sharing, archiving or review

## The one rule {#contribute-sourcing}

::: {.tada-warn}
**Separate what the papers say from what you are adding.**

If a claim comes from one of the three source papers, state that and cite it —
by author and year, so a reader can find it in [References](#references). If it
is your own practical advice, label it **wiki guidance**, as this wiki does
throughout.

This is the whole reason the wiki is trustworthy. A page that blends the two is
worse than no page.
:::

Concretely:

> The SORTEE guidelines require that code files are in an interoperable format
> (Guideline 3.4). ✅ *sourced, and pinpointed*
>
> Wiki guidance: in practice, the quickest way to check this is to open every
> file in a plain text editor before you deposit. ✅ *labelled as an addition*
>
> You must always use `.csv` for data. ❌ *unsourced, and stronger than the
> source*

## File layout {#contribute-layout}

```
TADA-Wiki/
├── index.Rmd              Welcome page (chapter order lives in _bookdown.yml)
├── 01-quickstart.Rmd      … one file per chapter, numbered in reading order
├── 11-references.Rmd
├── _bookdown.yml          Chapter list, output directory, labels
├── _output.yml            Theme, CSS, includes
├── render.R               Build script
├── assets/
│   ├── style.css          All styling. Tokens at the top; dark mode at the bottom
│   ├── tada.js            Turns `.tabset` sections into tabs
│   ├── head.html          Injected into <head> of every page
│   └── foot.html          Injected at the end of <body> of every page
├── templates/             Copy-and-fill templates for readers
├── papers/                The three source PDFs
└── docs/                  Rendered site — generated, do not edit by hand
```

## Adding a chapter {#contribute-chapter}

1. **Copy the template.**

   ```bash
   cp templates/page-template.Rmd 12-my-new-chapter.Rmd
   ```

2. **Give it a heading and an ID.** Every chapter starts with a level-1
   heading carrying an explicit ID, because other pages link to it:

   ```markdown
   # My new chapter {#my-new-chapter}
   ```

3. **Register it** in `_bookdown.yml`, in the position you want it to appear:

   ```yaml
   rmd_files:
     - "index.Rmd"
     ...
     - "12-my-new-chapter.Rmd"
     - "11-references.Rmd"   # keep references last
   ```

4. **Build and check.**

   ```bash
   Rscript render.R
   ```

   Open `docs/index.html`. The build fails loudly on a broken cross-reference,
   so a clean build is a real check.

## Writing conventions {#contribute-style}

### Cross-references {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Link by ID: `[Transferable](#transferable)`,
`[the four Rs](#review-four-rs)`. Give every section you might want to link to
an explicit `{#id}` — auto-generated IDs change when you edit a heading, and
silently break links.

### Callouts {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Four are defined in `assets/style.css`. Use them sparingly; a page of callouts
is a page with no emphasis at all.

```markdown
::: {.tada-key}
The short version — one paragraph that summarises the section.
:::

::: {.tada-tip}
Try this — a concrete, actionable suggestion.
:::

::: {.tada-warn}
Watch out — a common, costly mistake.
:::

::: {.tada-note}
Note — a caveat, exception, or aside.
:::
```

### Tabs {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Wrap the panes in a `.tabset` div. Each heading inside becomes a tab label, so
mark them `{.unlisted .unnumbered}` to keep them out of the contents listing and
out of the section numbering.

```markdown
::: {.tabset}

#### R {.unlisted .unnumbered}

...

#### Python {.unlisted .unnumbered}

...

:::
```

`assets/tada.js` finds any element with the `tabset` class, so putting
`{.tabset}` on a heading instead (`## How to do it {#some-id .tabset}`) also
works. The div form is used throughout this wiki because it makes the extent of
the tab group explicit.

With JavaScript disabled every pane simply renders in sequence, so never put
anything in a tab that the page depends on being hidden.

### Before / after code {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Use `::::` for the outer fence so the inner `:::` fences nest correctly.

````markdown
:::: {.tada-compare}
::: {.tada-before}
Before

```r
setwd("C:/Users/me/project")
```
:::

::: {.tada-after}
After

```r
library(here)
```
:::
::::
````

### Checklists {.unlisted .unnumbered}

End substantial chapters with one. Markdown task syntax, one item per line:

```markdown
- [ ] Something the reader can verify in under a minute
```

### Code chunks {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Chunks are set to `eval = FALSE` globally in `index.Rmd` — code on this wiki is
illustrative and is never executed at build time. If you genuinely need a chunk
to run, set `eval = TRUE` on that chunk *and* state the dependency in your pull
request, because it becomes a build requirement for everyone.

### Voice {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- Second person, present tense. "Save your code as `.R`", not "code should be
  saved".
- Say the thing, then say why. The *why* is what makes a guideline stick.
- Prefer concrete numbers over adjectives. "74% of archived R files failed to
  run" beats "many files fail to run".
- Assume the reader is a competent researcher who has never archived code
  before. Not a novice, not a software engineer.

## References {#contribute-references}

Add new sources to `11-references.Rmd`, alphabetically by first author, in the
existing format:

```markdown
**Author, A. B., & Author, C. D.** (Year). *Title of the work.* Journal
Volume: pages. <https://doi.org/…>
```

Include a DOI wherever one exists. If you cite something in a chapter, it must
appear in that list.

## Submitting {#contribute-submitting}

If this wiki lives in a git repository:

```bash
git checkout -b add-julia-guidance
git add 12-julia.Rmd _bookdown.yml 11-references.Rmd
git commit -m "Add Julia-specific transferability guidance"
git push -u origin add-julia-guidance
```

Then open a pull request describing **what you added** and **where it came
from** — sourced from a paper, or your own practice.

::: {.tada-note}
Once a repository URL is set in `_output.yml` (the `repo:` block, currently
commented out), bs4_book adds an **Edit this page** link to every chapter,
which is the fastest route for small corrections.
:::

### Before you submit {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- [ ] `Rscript render.R` completes without errors or warnings
- [ ] Every claim from a source paper is attributed; every addition of your own is labelled as wiki guidance
- [ ] New sources are in `11-references.Rmd`
- [ ] Every heading you link to has an explicit `{#id}`
- [ ] Cross-references resolve (click them in `docs/`)
- [ ] Chapter is registered in `_bookdown.yml`
- [ ] Checked in both light and dark mode, and at a narrow window width
- [ ] `docs/` changes are included in the commit, or excluded consistently — pick one and say which in the PR
